x: Flower was leading, closely followed by Carter, Rice, Taylor and Smith. Coming up the hill about 3 miles out, Carter had taken the lead and, running very strongly with that natural easy style of his, he was gradually dropping the rest of the field.
Our other men were at this time not doing too well, for Rice and Walker were in the 30's. They were, however, closely followed by Robertshaw, Mitchell and Cecil Penny.

He was followed by Allum and Footer together, with Carter, Shields, Flower, Patiences A. and R., and Rice in that order. There was little change as the runners crossed the Golf Links at the start of the second lap, but Alf Taylor and Syd Warboys had moved up slightly.

Webb 62, Rice 74, Allum 102. In 1930 the race was staged from Brighton Racecourse Stand, over a difficult course, with its ascents and descents of the Sussex Downs; but the finish found us jubilant at gaining third place for the first time, and optimistic about future years.

In a fast start Chantler was the best away, but was soon headed by Syd Warboys moving in his best style and taking the field along at a fast pace for about ¾ mile, when Tom Carter moved up to take the lead, followed closely by Allum, Shields, Rice and J.

Allum, Rice and myself made the pace at the start and at half-way we were still together. Arthur was setting a fast pace and I knew that my only hope was to keep with him; Bill Rice then fell back and we came across from the Flagstaff, running shoulder to shoulder.

Our boys were placed: Allum 6, Scrimshaw 9, Rice 10, Shields 11—36 points. At the conclusion of three events we have scored 17 out of a possible 18 points and have a 4½ points lead over the next club, Polytechnic Harriers.

In the 4 x 220 yards we were fourth (Mewes, Bennett, Stower, Christie), a position we also filled in the 4 x 440 yards event (Jones, Stower, Clubb, Pack). We gained points in the Mile through the efforts of Rice, second, and Shields, fourth.

When the field was sighted, for the turn home, Carter was leading the pack, running comfortably, followed by Ring, Shields, Rice, and J. Flower, with our "South of the Thames" Juniors, Martin, Saunders and Chantler, close on their heels.
Then come Jack Flower, Shields, Allum, Ring D. Patience, Taylor, Rice, Shaw, R.
Bill Rice again took this stage for us and as the representative of last year's winning team received the letter of greeting from Sir S. Killick, Lord Mayor of London, to Councillor S.

We congratulate Birchfield upon scoring one over us; and both teams were delighted with the match—and, may it be said, are eager for the next. Jim Ginty, of ours, led the field home in 14 min. 43 sec., and Ring and Rice did well to finish third and fourth.
In the absence of Rice the Two Miles went to Hunter in 9.20, with veteran McCluskey doing 9.25. The High Jump and Pole Vault went at 6ft. 6in. and 14ft. respectively.
